dataset.description: SDR-based radio frequency measurements are expected to be obtained in a controlled Open RAN lab setting as part of the CORA project make up the dataset. It records the characteristics of specific spectrum bands in the time and frequency domains under different network configurations. The dataset's main goals are to provide baseline measurements for performance benchmarking and to facilitate the development, training, and validation of machine learning algorithms for dynamic spectrum sensing and control in private 5G networks.

distribution.title:
The data will be gathered to aid the creation and assessment of cognitive spectrum sensing and control systems in private 5G networks based on Open RAN. It directly supports the goals of the project concerning QoS-oriented performance evaluation, machine learning-assisted decision-making, SDR-based spectrum sensing, and Open RAN benchmarking.

Using SDR platforms for spectrum sensing and Open RAN components for network performance monitoring, the data will be collected from controlled laboratory experiments carried out in a private 5G test environment based on Open RAN.

dataset.title: CORA Open RAN Radio Environment Measurements

dmp.description:
The CORA project is set to produce experimental research data that will mainly be relevant to SDR based spectrum sensing, Open RAN setups, and machine learning algorithms for spectrum control in private 5G networks. The main data collected will be radio frequency measurements, related network performance metrics, and the derived datasets that have been used for analysis and model validation. Data will be generated in controlled laboratory experiments carried out at the Open RAN Research Laboratory, Riga Technical University.

Data will be saved in open, widely used formats (e. g. , binary files for raw SDR captures with a detailed documentation, and structured formats such as CSV, JSON, and HDF5 for processed data and metadata) to provide easy access and ensure interoperability. Dataset, level metadata will adopt conventional research metadata standards (e. g. , Dublin Core) and will be further supplemented with  documentation and project specific technical metadata, which describes the experimental conditions, SDR configurations, and Open RAN testbed setups.
